images.caption: Figure 1:Illustration of Cross-Context Binder Design.Multi-state (MS)design (left) focuses on maintaining interface compatibility across the target’s conformational landscape, preventing the loss of affinity when the target reshapes during functional switching.Multi-target (MT)design (right) focuses on multi-specificity, where a single sequence is optimized to engage similar epitopes on distinct proteins with high binding affinity.

Figure 2:Training pipeline of I3CD.We concatenate clean target signals (blue tokens) with noisy binder signals (orange tokens) and feed them into the proposed I3CD paradigm to learn the joint dependencies of target and binder via discrete and continuous flow matching. Crucially,the binder’s sequence and structure are corrupted using decoupled noise schedules (t,t~t,\tilde{t}), enabling the model to effectively capture the intricate sequence-structure interplay and facilitating future cross-context binder design.

Figure 3:Illustration of MoPS.By leveraging forward folding as a bridging mechanism, MoPS interleaves the sampling trajectories of different conformations. This enables simultaneous sequence-structure co-design across multiple binder states. The nameChamaileonembodies our vision of AI-designed binders as chameleons, capable of adaptively adjusting their conformations in response to the context.

Figure 4:Illustration of beam search.In each time interval, the strategy retains only the highest-scoring candidate (solid line) while discarding less likely paths (dashed lines), ensuring efficient navigation toward the global optimum.

Figure 5:Qualitative results ofChamaileonon cross-context binder design.For each case, the target protein is shown in deep blue-red spectrum with warmer color (red) indicating higher structural deviations, while the designed binder is shown inBinder State I(blue) andBinder State II(pink).
The “Aligned” column displays the superposition of both states, with structures aligned based on the target backbones to highlight how binder conformations adapt different contexts.
Figure 6:Data collection pipeline.(a) Construction of the I3CD training set. (b) Construction of the CROSS benchmark.

Figure 7:Scalability of MoPS with respect to the number of conformations.By cyclically alternating among target states, MoPS extends binder co-design to an arbitrary number of conformations without incurring additional computational overhead.
